```420:457:miataru/views/iPhone/Devices Views/iPhone_DeviceMapView.swift
@ViewBuilder
private func updateButton() -> some View {
    if #available(iOS 26.0, *) {
        Button(action: {
            Task { await fetchLocation(resetZoomToSettings: true) }
        }) {
            Image(systemName: "arrow.clockwise")
                .font(.system(size: 16, weight: .semibold))
                .frame(width: 34, height: 34)
                .foregroundStyle(Color.primary)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(NSLocalizedString("refresh_device_location", comment: "Refresh device location"))
        .overlay(Circle().stroke(Color.primary.opacity(0.15), lineWidth: 1))
        .shadow(radius: 1)
        .glassEffect(in: .capsule)
    } else {
        Button(action: {
            Task { await fetchLocation(resetZoomToSettings: true) }
        }) {
            Image(systemName: "arrow.clockwise")
                .font(.system(size: 16, weight: .semibold))
                .frame(width: 34, height: 34)
                .foregroundStyle(Color.primary)
        }
        .buttonStyle(.plain)
        .accessibilityLabel(NSLocalizedString("refresh_device_location", comment: "Refresh device location"))
        .overlay(Circle().stroke(Color.primary.opacity(0.15), lineWidth: 1))
        .shadow(radius: 1)
        .background(.ultraThinMaterial)
        .clipShape(Circle())
    }
}
```

Ich habe es so angepasst:
- iOS 26+: Glas auf einer runden Rechteckfläche, Symbol darüber in klarer Primärfarbe.
- < iOS 26: `.ultraThinMaterial`-Hintergrund + runder Clip, Symbol in Primärfarbe.
- Overlay-Rand und leichter Schatten für den klaren „glassy“ Rand.
- Accessibility-Label wieder aktiviert.
